description: My furnace makes a loud booming sound a few seconds after it kicks on, then heats normally. It started doing this last week.
rationale: Delayed-ignition boom can indicate a dirty burner or gas buildup; not same-day but worth a tech soon for safety.

description: The air coming out of my vents smells faintly musty when the AC first turns on, then it goes away after a minute or two.
rationale: Classic evaporator-coil mildew smell; a DIY coil cleaner and filter swap usually handles it. Watch if it worsens.

description: I haven't changed my furnace filter in probably eight months and airflow from the vents seems weaker than it used to be.
rationale: Overdue filter is the most common DIY HVAC fix; weak airflow is the expected symptom, not an emergency.

description: My carbon monoxide detector went off near the furnace and the furnace is running right now. I have a slight headache.
rationale: Active CO alarm plus symptoms is a same-day life-safety event; deviates to safety tag over hvac per spec allowance.

description: My central AC stopped cooling. The outdoor unit fan spins but the air inside is just room temperature, and the line going into the house has ice on it.
rationale: Iced line set usually means low refrigerant or airflow problem; needs a tech within days, not life-threatening.

description: The thermostat screen is blank and won't turn on. I tried pressing buttons but nothing happens.
rationale: Most often dead thermostat batteries or a tripped float switch — a homeowner can swap batteries first before calling anyone.

description: There's a little condensation drip from the AC unit in my attic onto the drain pan, but the pan isn't overflowing.
rationale: Drain pan catching normal condensate; clearing the condensate line with vinegar is a routine DIY task. Watch for overflow.

description: My mini-split's remote shows an error code E6 and the indoor unit beeps three times but won't start cooling.
rationale: Manufacturer error code on a sealed-refrigerant system points to a tech diagnostic; not urgent but won't self-resolve.

description: One bedroom is always 5-6 degrees warmer than the rest of the house no matter the season. It's been like this since we moved in.
rationale: Long-standing balance issue; adjusting the supply damper or vent is a comfort tweak, not a defect. Low urgency.

description: Water is actively pouring out from under my kitchen sink and pooling on the cabinet floor. I shut the cabinet valve and it slowed but didn't stop.
rationale: Active uncontrolled leak with continuing flow after shutoff is same-day; risks cabinet and subfloor damage fast.

description: My bathroom faucet drips about once every two seconds even when fully closed. It's been doing it for a couple weeks.
rationale: A worn washer or cartridge; a homeowner can replace it for a few dollars. Wastes water but no immediate harm.

description: The toilet in the guest bath runs constantly — I can hear water trickling into the bowl and the tank never fully fills.
rationale: Flapper or fill-valve issue; cheap DIY part and clear instructions. Soon because it silently wastes a lot of water.

description: My water heater has a small puddle forming underneath it and there's a faint rusty stain on the tank near the bottom.
rationale: Tank-bottom rust and weeping usually means the tank is failing; replacement is a plumber job before it ruptures.

description: My kitchen drain is slow and gurgles, and the sink takes about a minute to fully empty after I run the tap.
rationale: Partial clog; a plunger, baking soda, or a hand auger is typical DIY. Annoying but low risk.

description: There's a brown water stain on my ceiling directly below the upstairs bathroom and it feels slightly damp to the touch.
rationale: Active hidden leak behind drywall; needs a plumber to find the source. Deviates to interior tag — the visible damage is a ceiling.

description: My hot water ran out much faster than usual this morning and the water never got more than lukewarm at any tap.
rationale: Failed heating element or thermostat on the water heater; a tech repair, not an emergency but disrupts daily use.

description: When I flush the toilet, water backs up into the bathtub drain in the same bathroom. Multiple drains seem affected.
rationale: Cross-fixture backup indicates a main sewer-line clog; risk of sewage overflow makes it same/next-day for a plumber.

description: My showerhead has hard white mineral crust around the holes and the spray is splitting into weird directions.
rationale: Limescale buildup; a vinegar soak fully fixes it. No urgency, purely a nuisance.

description: I smell burning plastic near an outlet in my living room and the wall plate feels warm. Nothing is plugged in right now.
rationale: Warm outlet plus burning smell is an active fire hazard; cut the breaker and get an electrician same-day. Safety tag deviation.

description: One outlet in my kitchen stopped working but the others on the wall are fine. The lights still work too.
rationale: Almost certainly a tripped GFCI that needs a reset button press; a homeowner can check before calling anyone.

description: The lights in half my house flicker whenever the microwave or hair dryer runs, and it's gotten more noticeable lately.
rationale: Whole-circuit flicker under load can point to a loose neutral or panel issue; needs an electrician within days.

description: My breaker for the bedroom trips every couple of days for no obvious reason and I have to go reset it.
rationale: Repeated tripping signals an overload or fault the breaker is protecting against; diagnosis is an electrician's job.

description: A light switch in my hallway buzzes faintly and feels warm when the light is on. The light itself works fine.
rationale: Warm/buzzing switch suggests a loose connection or failing device — a fire-risk precursor, replace soon via an electrician.

description: I want to swap a standard light switch for a dimmer in my dining room. The wiring looks like a single switch with two wires.
rationale: Straightforward like-for-like device swap with the breaker off; a confident homeowner can do it. No urgency.

description: Half the outlets in my garage went dead at once. The breaker isn't tripped and there's a GFCI outlet I haven't checked yet.
rationale: Downstream of a tripped GFCI is the likely cause; resetting it is a simple DIY first step before escalating.

description: My ceiling fan wobbles a lot on high speed and makes a clicking sound, but it still spins and the light works.
rationale: Wobble is usually blade balance or loose mounting screws; a balance kit and tightening is routine DIY.

description: There are scorch marks and a melted look around the prongs of my dryer's 240V outlet, and the dryer keeps cutting out.
rationale: Melted high-amperage outlet is an imminent fire hazard; stop using it and call an electrician same-day. Safety tag.

description: There's a hairline crack in the drywall above my doorway, maybe a foot long. It looks the same as it did a year ago.
rationale: Stable hairline drywall crack over a door is normal settling; spackle and paint. Interior tag deviation per spec.

description: I noticed a diagonal crack in my foundation wall in the basement that's about a quarter inch wide and seems to be getting wider.
rationale: A widening quarter-inch diagonal foundation crack warrants a structural eval soon; not collapse-imminent but progressing.

description: My upstairs floor feels bouncy and slopes noticeably toward one corner of the room. A marble rolls across it on its own.
rationale: Sloping bouncy floor suggests joist or support failure; needs a structural assessment soon. Framing → exterior per map.

description: A few of my interior doors have started sticking and won't latch properly over the past couple of months.
rationale: Seasonal humidity or minor settling; planing or hinge adjustment is DIY. Worth watching in case settling accelerates.

description: There's a large stair-step crack running through the mortar of my exterior brick wall and one brick has shifted outward.
rationale: Stair-step mortar cracking with displacement points to foundation movement; a pro evaluation within weeks.

description: The deck attached to my house feels wobbly when several people stand on it and I can see the ledger board pulling slightly away from the wall.
rationale: A separating deck ledger is a collapse hazard under load; stop using it and get it inspected immediately.

description: Some of the trim and baseboard in my hallway has visible nail-pop bumps where the nails are pushing the paint out.
rationale: Nail pops are normal in newer framing as wood dries; reset and spot-paint. Purely cosmetic. Interior tag.

description: A support post in my crawlspace looks like it's no longer fully touching the beam above it — there's a small gap at the top.
rationale: A gapping support post means load isn't transferring properly; structural pro needed soon to shim/jack correctly.

description: After the windstorm last night I can see three or four shingles are missing from the front slope of my roof.
rationale: Exposed underlayment invites leaks; a roofer should patch within days before the next rain, but no active interior damage yet.

description: Water is dripping from my ceiling into a bucket every time it rains hard, and the drip has gotten faster over the last two storms.
rationale: An accelerating active roof leak risks structural and mold damage fast; tarp or emergency repair same/next-day.

description: The shingles on my roof look a bit faded and there's some granule loss collecting in the gutters, but no leaks that I know of.
rationale: Granule loss signals aging shingles; worth a roofer's check at next convenience to plan replacement. Not urgent.

description: My gutters are overflowing during rain and I can see them packed full of leaves and debris from the ground.
rationale: Clogged gutters are a classic DIY clean-out; overflow can harm fascia over time so don't ignore, but low urgency.

description: There's a section of flashing around my chimney that's lifted up and you can see a gap underneath it.
rationale: Lifted chimney flashing is a common leak entry point; reseal soon via a roofer before water intrudes.

description: I see a small patch of green moss growing on the north-facing section of my asphalt shingle roof.
rationale: Light moss on shingles is mostly cosmetic early on; gentle treatment and zinc strips are DIY. Low urgency.

description: A few inches of my roof's ridge cap shingles have curled up at the edges and one corner looks like it could lift in wind.
rationale: Curling ridge caps are vulnerable to wind uplift and leaks; a roofer should secure them within weeks.

description: I noticed a faint dark stain spreading on the plywood in my attic right under where a roofing nail pokes through.
rationale: Stain around a nail can be minor condensation or a slow weep; have a roofer assess, watch for growth. Not urgent yet.

description: My pool water has turned cloudy and slightly green over the past few days even though the pump is running.
rationale: Early algae/chemistry imbalance; shock and rebalance chemicals is standard DIY pool care. No pool enum value → other.

description: The pool pump is making a loud grinding noise and the motor feels very hot to the touch when running.
rationale: Grinding + overheating motor risks seizing; a pool tech should service the bearings/motor soon. Specialist domain → other.

description: My pool's water level drops about two inches a day, more than evaporation would explain, and the ground near one side feels soggy.
rationale: Rapid loss with soggy ground points to a plumbing or shell leak; needs a leak-detection specialist within days.

description: There's a small crack in the plaster on the step of my pool, maybe two inches long. It doesn't seem to be leaking.
rationale: Surface plaster crack should be watched and patched by a pool pro before it deepens; not urgent without leakage.

description: My saltwater chlorinator shows a 'low salt' warning even though I added salt last week, and chlorine output seems weak.
rationale: Often a dirty salt cell or a sensor reading that resolves after circulation; cleaning the cell is DIY. Low urgency.

description: I see exposed wiring near my pool's underwater light where the conduit has come loose at the niche.
rationale: Exposed wiring near water is an electrocution hazard; cut power and get a licensed pro immediately. Safety tag deviation.

description: The skimmer basket on my pool has a crack and a piece broke off, so debris is getting past it into the pump basket.
rationale: A cracked skimmer basket is a cheap drop-in replacement part; trivial DIY, no real urgency.

description: My pool heater won't ignite — it clicks a few times then shows an ignition fault code on the display.
rationale: Gas pool-heater ignition faults involve gas and combustion; a specialist should diagnose. Soon, not safety-critical if heater is off.

description: I'm seeing a steady trail of small ants marching along my kitchen counter to a spot near the sink every morning.
rationale: Common nuisance ants respond to DIY baits and sealing entry points; no pest enum value → other. Low urgency.

description: I found small piles of what look like sawdust under a wooden beam in my basement and a few tiny holes in the wood.
rationale: Frass and bore holes suggest wood-boring insects or termites; a pest pro should inspect soon to limit structural damage.

description: I hear scratching and scurrying sounds in my attic at night and found some droppings near the insulation.
rationale: Rodents in the attic can chew wiring (fire risk) and breed quickly; pro removal soon. Pest has no enum → other.

description: There's a single small spider web in the corner of my garage ceiling and I see one spider in it.
rationale: An isolated garage spider is harmless; knock down the web. Essentially no action needed. Pest → other.

description: I noticed a wasp nest about the size of a softball forming under the eave right next to my front door.
rationale: An active wasp nest by a high-traffic door is a sting risk; pro removal soon, or careful DIY for the confident. Leaning hire.

description: We've started seeing several cockroaches at night in the kitchen even though we keep it clean, and there were a couple in a cabinet.
rationale: Visible roaches by day/night usually mean an established population; professional treatment is most effective. Soon.

description: There are a few small moths flying around my pantry and I found tiny webbing inside an old bag of flour.
rationale: Pantry moths are handled by tossing infested goods, cleaning, and traps — all DIY. Annoying, low urgency.

description: I think a small animal, maybe a squirrel, has been getting into a gap where my roofline meets the gutter — I see chew marks.
rationale: Wildlife entry into the roof structure should be excluded by a pro to avoid nesting and damage. Soon, not same-day.

description: After heavy rain, water pools in the same low spot in my backyard and takes two days to drain, near the foundation.
rationale: Standing water near the foundation can lead to seepage; regrading/drainage is a soon hire to protect the structure.

description: A large branch on the oak tree near my house cracked in the last storm and is hanging down over my driveway.
rationale: A hanging cracked branch over a driveway is a falling hazard to people and cars; arborist removal same/next-day.

description: Some patches of my lawn have turned brown and dry while the rest is green, despite regular watering.
rationale: Brown patches are usually fungus, grubs, or uneven coverage — DIY treatment and seeding. Purely aesthetic.

description: My irrigation system has one zone where a sprinkler head is broken off and water just bubbles up out of the ground there.
rationale: A broken sprinkler head is a cheap screw-in replacement; common DIY. Wastes water, so don't wait forever.

description: The soil along my house's foundation has eroded and now slopes back toward the house instead of away from it.
rationale: Negative grade directs water at the foundation; regrading soon prevents basement moisture. Often a pro/landscaper job.

description: A few of my retaining wall blocks near the patio have shifted forward and the wall bows out slightly in the middle.
rationale: A bowing retaining wall is starting to fail and can collapse; assessment/repair soon by a pro. Not yet imminent.

description: My wooden fence has one post that wobbles and leans because the base seems loose in the ground.
rationale: A single loose fence post can be reset in concrete by a handy homeowner; low urgency, mostly cosmetic/functional.

description: Tree roots have started lifting and cracking a section of my concrete walkway, creating a raised tripping edge.
rationale: Root-heaved walkway is a trip hazard worth addressing; root pruning/slab work is usually a pro. Watch the edge.

description: The caulk around my bathtub has cracked and pulled away from the wall in a few spots, leaving a small gap.
rationale: Failed tub caulk lets water behind the wall over time; re-caulking is easy DIY. Watch for any soft drywall. Interior deviation.

description: One of my interior doors won't stay open — it slowly swings shut on its own because the frame seems out of level.
rationale: A self-closing door is fixed by bending a hinge pin slightly; trivial DIY. No real consequence. Interior deviation.

description: My garage door reverses immediately every time it tries to close, even though nothing is blocking the path.
rationale: Usually misaligned safety sensors at the base; realigning/cleaning them is DIY. Soon because the door is unusable.

description: There's a musty smell and some black speckling on the grout in the corner of my bathroom that keeps coming back after I clean it.
rationale: Surface mildew in a damp bathroom; clean and improve ventilation. Watch in case it indicates a deeper moisture issue. Interior.

description: My smoke detector chirps once every minute and won't stop even though the light still blinks.
rationale: Chirping means a low battery or end-of-life unit; swapping the battery is DIY, but a working detector matters → soon. Safety tag.

description: The paint on my hallway ceiling is peeling and flaking in a small area, though the surface underneath feels dry.
rationale: Dry-surface peeling paint is a scrape, prime, and repaint job; purely cosmetic DIY. Interior deviation.

description: My dishwasher leaves a pool of water in the bottom after every cycle and dishes on the top rack come out still dirty.
rationale: Standing water + poor cleaning often means a clogged filter or spray arm; cleaning them is DIY. Appliance tag.

description: My refrigerator isn't keeping things as cold as it used to and the coils on the back are coated in thick dust.
rationale: Dusty condenser coils reduce cooling efficiency; vacuuming them is routine DIY maintenance. Appliance tag.
